subject: High latency + token errors on Orbital AI dedicated pool — incident update & post-incident wrap-up
messages:
From: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@orbital.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: High latency & token errors on dedicated pool - urgent

Hi Camila / Redwood ops,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx errors and request timeouts from our dedicated pool (orbital-dedicated-1) starting ~08:50 PST. The request paths for some of our real-time features are timing out (~6–12s) and a subset of requests are returning token-stream errors (partial outputs with "token_drop" logs). This is impacting our customer-facing chat product (sev P1).

What we have observed:
- Spike in queue depth and per-request latency at 08:49–08:57 PST
- 502 / 504s for ~8% of calls to /v1/generate between 08:50–09:05
- Sample request IDs: req_8812, req_8830

We've attached a short trace capture (orbital_request_traces.log). Please advise next steps and whether you can fail traffic to a hosted fallback while you investigate — we need a mitigation ASAP.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Gomez
Head of Infrastructure, Orbital AI
Alyssa@orbital.ai


From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:25:31 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency & token errors on dedicated pool - urgent

Thanks Alyssa — we see the alerts on our side and have declared an incident. Ben (cc) is the incident lead.

Immediate actions we've kicked off:
- Engaging the Dedicated control plane to check node health and active warmup tasks
- Pulling the sample traces you attached
- Preparing a hosted fallback route in case manual failover is needed (we can flip a routing rule to send new requests to a compatible hosted model variant)

Helpful asks for us while we triage:
- If you can share the full request ID for 8812 and 8830 that will speed debugging (we have partial traces)
- If you have a short timeseries of QPS and token rate for the last 30m, please paste it inline or attach

I'll update in ~30m with what we find. We'll include a remediation plan and an ETA for a safe fallback if needed.

—Camila

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@orbital.ai>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 11:40:12 -0800
Subject: Incident update: root cause and immediate remediation (Orbital AI)

Alyssa / team — quick technical update and what we changed. TL;DR: autoscaler predicate + warmup evaluation edge case caused delayed node readiness which led to temporary queueing and partial fallback not firing. Service stabilized after manual capacity increase and rebalancing at ~11:15 PST.

What we saw (timeline highlights):
- 08:47 PST: sharp increase in incoming QPS from Orbital production (warm traffic pattern change)
- 08:49 PST: autoscaler evaluated warmup predicate and scheduled 3 additional reserved nodes; provisioning took longer than expected (6–7 minutes) due to a recent controller optimization that adjusted preflight checks
- 08:56–09:05 PST: queue depth rose and per-request latencies spiked; some streaming sessions returned token-drop partial outputs (we captured those traces)
- 09:05 PST: internal routing policy attempted to activate hosted fallback, but a filter mismatch prevented automatic activation for a small subset of tenant routes
- 09:25 PST: Camila opened the ticket and we performed an emergency manual allocation to the dedicated pool
- 11:15 PST: manual rebalancing and node warmup finished; latency returned to baseline

Remediation performed (immediate):
- Manually increased reserved nodes by +4 for orbital-dedicated-1 and forced warmup to complete
- Repaired the fallback filter so the hosted-route trigger will match Orbital tenant rules
- Purged queued backlog and restarted a subset of serving workers to clear token-stream state

Current status:
- Metrics show median latency back to baseline; error rate reduced to <0.1% over last 30m
- We continue to monitor the tenant-specific queueing and token error telemetry for 24h

Next steps / follow-up:
- We'll deliver a written post-incident summary with RCA and concrete action items by EOD Thursday (Feb 18)
- Camila / Laura will follow up about commercial remediation (credit) and any contract implications

Attachments: sample_trace_8812.json (excerpt)

Apologies for the impact — Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Reliability
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa@orbital.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Orbital AI dedicated-pool event — post-incident wrap-up and action items

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for your patience while we investigated. Below is the post-incident wrap-up, root cause, and our proposed remedial actions. We included a short timeline and next steps for both engineering and commercial teams.

Executive summary:
Between 08:47–11:15 PST on Feb 14, Orbital AI experienced elevated latency and a small rate (~8%) of token-stream errors on your dedicated pool (orbital-dedicated-1). A combination of delayed node warmup (caused by a controller preflight change) and an edge-case mismatch in the hosted-fallback filter prevented an automatic, tenant-scoped fallback for several request paths. Manual capacity allocation and forced warmups restored normal service by 11:15 PST.

Full timeline (UTC and local PST):
- 2027-02-14 16:47:00 UTC / 08:47 PST — Sharp QPS increase observed
- 2027-02-14 16:49:00 UTC / 08:49 PST — Autoscaler scheduled additional reserved nodes
- 2027-02-14 16:56:00 UTC / 08:56 PST — Queue depth exceeded 75th percentile; token-stream anomalies begin
- 2027-02-14 17:05:00 UTC / 09:05 PST — Partial hosted-fallback attempted; filter mismatch prevented activation for some routes
- 2027-02-14 18:15:00 UTC / 11:15 PST — Manual rebalancing and forced warmup completed; metrics returned to baseline

Root cause (RCA):
1) Controller preflight change: a recent optimization added additional readiness gates during node provisioning; under a rapid warmup pattern this extended provisioning latency by ~4–7 minutes in some cases.
2) Fallback filter edge-case: the tenant-scoped routing filter did not match requests with certain downstream headers that Orbital uses for session affinity, preventing automatic activation of the hosted fallback for those sessions.

Action items and timelines:
- Immediate (within 48h): revert the strict preflight gate for autoscaler warmup on reserved pools while we complete compatibility testing (owner: Serving Runtime)
- Short term (2 weeks): patch routing filter logic so hosted-fallback covers the header patterns used by Orbital; create a smoke test that simulates session-affinity headers (owner: Routing team)
- Medium term (1 month): add a canary rollout for controller preflight changes + a synthetic warmup workload to validate provisioning latency under increased QPS (owner: Infra)
- Long term (quarterly): add a dedicated capacity drill and update runbooks to include token-stream integrity checks and forced-rollback paths (owner: Reliability & Product)

Commercial remediation:
- We are proposing a 20% credit on Orbital's Feb invoice and two weeks of free burst capacity on the dedicated pool to cover any residual risk while the short-term fixes land. Laura (cc) will coordinate credits and billing details.

Evidence and artifacts attached:
- postmortem_timeline.csv (detailed metric slices)
- sample_trace_8812.json (trace excerpt)
- preliminary_capture.zip (trace bundle)

Request: please confirm receipt and whether the credit proposal covers your immediate needs. Also let us know preferred times for a 30-minute technical walk-through next week (we recommend Tue/Wed in the morning PST).

Thanks again — we'll keep the monitoring window open and share progress on the action items.

Best,
